findings.title: Parameter update validation and installation
findings.summary: FinalizeBlock may return a complete or partial consensus-parameter update whose response is durable before the candidate is validated and installed. ConsensusParams.Update copies the current parameters and replaces each non-nil subrecord, after which ValidateBasic and ValidateUpdate gate acceptance. A rejected candidate should leave the input state unchanged even though its FinalizeBlock response may already be persisted, while an accepted candidate should become active at height H+1. Confirmation should examine the validation and error paths through updateState and BlockExecutor.ApplyBlock.

findings.title: Ordered durable boundaries during block application
findings.summary: Block application crosses several ordered durable boundaries: the decided block is stored, FinalizeBlock runs, its response is saved, the application commits, and CometBFT state is saved. A process crash can therefore expose different combinations of block-store, response, application, and state-store progress. The state store persists the latest response separately from the later batch that records state and next-height consensus parameters. Confirmation should inspect each crash window for inconsistent height or parameter state at restart.

findings.title: Height-matrix startup replay
findings.summary: Startup selects among app-only replay, real-application last-block replay, saved-response mock replay, and no replay according to application, block-store, and state-store heights. Unsupported height relationships are rejected, while supported cases take different paths for application progress and CometBFT state mutation. Historical app-only replay uses ExecCommitBlock, whereas a final state-mutating replay reuses ApplyBlock and may consume the persisted FinalizeBlock response. Confirmation should exercise the height matrix and verify that normal operation begins only after the durable heights and consensus-parameter state are synchronized.
